references.text: Describes the same principle that the manslayer shall remain in a city of refuge until he stands trial before the assembly.
States that the manslayer must stay in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest, after which he may return to his property.
Repeats that the manslayer must remain in the city of refuge until the high priest dies, and only then can he return to his land.
Describes the process where the manslayer presents his case before the elders of the city at the city gate.
Mentions the office of the high priest and his role in Israel.
Speaks about fleeing to seize the hope set before us, a spiritual parallel to the city of refuge.
